Sedition

sih-DISH-un · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Sedition is conduct or speech inciting people to rebel against the authority of a state or government.

The pamphlets calling for an armed uprising against the king were quickly seized and burned as sedition.

Worked Example

The general was arrested and charged with sedition after secretly encouraging soldiers to turn against the government that commanded them.

Sedition specifically targets government authority -- it's a serious legal and political charge, not just any rebellious attitude.

How Sedition Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rebellion

rebellion: open resistance or defiance against authority

subversion

subversion: secret efforts to weaken or overthrow an established system

Antonyms

loyalty

loyalty: faithful support and allegiance

conformity

conformity: behavior that follows accepted standards or rules

How Strong Is It? — dissent → treason → sedition

dissent vs. sedition

dissent vs. sedition: Dissent is open disagreement with an official policy, without necessarily urging rebellion.

treason vs. sedition

treason vs. sedition: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, especially by attempting to overthrow the government -- even more severe than sedition.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of sedition.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — se-/sed-

prefix — se-/sed-: apart, aside -- the same piece that starts sequester and separate (Latin)

root (not standalone) — -ition

root (not standalone) — -ition: a going -- not a standalone English word on its own (Latin itio, from ire, 'to go')

Put it together

Put it together: Sedition comes from Latin se- ('apart') + itio ('a going') -- literally 'a going apart.' It names speech or action meant to make people break away from lawful authority.

Use the root in a new word: sequester

Use the root in a new word: sequester: The jury was sequestered in a hotel for the remainder of the trial to avoid outside influence.

Word Choice

Sedition is a serious legal and political term -- it describes speech or action that incites rebellion against a government, and it shows up most often in news, history, and law rather than everyday conversation.
